title: Counteranchor crafting — daily jot
content:
Purpose:
Quick-running notebook-style notes for a tiny prompt pattern I am tentatively calling 'counteranchor' — deliberate negative anchors included in prompt context to reduce hallucination drift and brittle role-swaps.

Background / intuition:
- When giving positive exemplars, model often over-generalizes a style/format and hallucinates required fields or invents facts to satisfy pattern.
- A counteranchor is an explicit example that demonstrates a *wrong* or undesired completion with short rationale (e.g. "DO NOT do X because Y"). The goal: make the model internalize a narrow boundary.
- Counteranchors are not adversarial inputs; they are compact negative exemplars placed alongside positive examples in few-shot sets.

Key hypotheses to test (quick):
1) Counteranchors reduce confident hallucinations for extraction tasks (dates, places, numeric values).
2) They help with role-stability: model less likely to 'role-play' beyond instructions when a counteranchor shows an obvious role-violation.
3) Too many counteranchors -> confusion / overcorrection (model starts refusing to answer). Need a balance.

Experiment matrix (mini):
- Task A (fact extraction from short bios): baseline 3 positive shots vs. 3+1 counteranchor vs. 3 + 2 small counteranchors. Measure precision/false-positive on extracted fields.
- Task B (instruction-following / API generation): positive fewshots vs. with counteranchor showing a broken API snippet and note. Measure malformed outputs.
- Task C (style-preservation across context switch): chain of user messages, insert counteranchor showing what *not* to do in switch. Observe role drift.

Draft few-shot templates (compact) — format: [PROMPT HEADER]
-- Positive exemplar 1:
Input: "Bio: \nSam, product manager. Loves skiing. Joined 2019."
Output: { name: Sam, role: product manager, interests: [skiing], join_year: 2019 }
-- Positive exemplar 2:
Input: "Bio: \nDr Lee, cardiologist, teaches at U of P, trained 2008."
Output: { name: Dr Lee, role: cardiologist, affiliation: University of P, trained_year: 2008 }
-- Counteranchor (explicit negative):
Input: "Bio: \nAlex — likes hiking; used to work in sales."
BadOutput: { name: Alex, role: <INVENTED: CTO>, affiliation: <INVENTED: Startup X>, join_year: 2013 }
Rationale: "Do NOT invent titles or affiliations when not present; return only fields explicitly supported by the input."

Notes on phrasing: keep counteranchor tiny (1–2 lines) and prefaced by cue words: "BadOutput", "Example of wrong completion", "DO NOT". Try table vs inline — initial thought: inline reduces token overhead.

Observed failure modes during quick manual runs (v0):
- Model sometimes mimics the counteranchor format exactly, producing "BadOutput" label as output. Need to instruct model to produce canonical good JSON only.
- When counteranchor is too punitive ("NEVER"), model refuses to fill optional fields even when evidence exists. So soften language: "Prefer not to invent" or include short rationale instead of absolute ban.
- Token budget: adding counteranchors increases prompt size; automated selection needed to keep per-request tokens < 512 for hosted tier tests.

Micro design rules (draft):
- At most 1 counteranchor per 3 positive shots.
- Counteranchor must: 1) show the error, 2) show a one-line rationale, 3) be labeled clearly as "wrong example".
- Prefer "soft negatives": show the wrong output but then add "Correct behavior:" with 1-line correct output to anchor both sides.

Prompt variant sketches (do quick A/B while tuning):
A) Inline negative then corrected example (counteranchor + correct)
B) Negative listed in a separate "Notes on common mistakes" paragraph after shots
C) No explicit labels (lean on natural language rationale), to test whether labels cause label-mimic failure.

Quick checklist for runs:
- [ ] baseline run (3 pos) on 100 bios (sample set: /data/bio-sample-100.csv)
- [ ] 3pos + 1 counteranchor (hard label)
- [ ] 3pos + 1 counteranchor (soft label + correct)
- [ ] record precision/recall, avg token length, failure cases (save 10 counterexamples)

Logging / artifacts to save per run:
- prompt text (redacted PII), model+size, temperature, top-p, max_tokens, date/time
- 50 failure examples + why (inverted meaning / invented field / label leak)
- short note: "did model output BadOutput label?" boolean

To-dos (next steps):
- pick 3 candidate models for quick runs: rwd-medium-2025, open-compat-gpt2xl, rwd-llama-q8 (priority order).
- script to swap in/out counteranchor block (simple templating) — Ravi to help with small CLI.
- set up tiny dashboard in sheet for metrics (precision, hallucination-rate, token-cost).

Slack threads / references I should check before heavy runs:
- #prompt-engineering (thread: "negative examples technique")
- GH issues: GH-PR-4521 (small script for prompt templating)

Random jotty notes:
- Might combine with prefix caching: store counteranchor once in account-level prefix so per-request copy can be smaller (but watch caching semantics across customers).
- For private deployments, counteranchor patterns could be an opt-in config (teams may dislike negative examples showing internal policies).
- Consider automated heuristic: include counteranchor only when input confidence is below threshold (i.e., model predicts lower certainty). But that's circular — need supervisor model.

Simple example final template (compact):
Instruction: Extract name, role, affiliation, join_year. If field not present, omit it. Do not invent titles or affiliations.

Fewshots:
[POS1] Input: "Bio: Sam, product manager, joined 2019"
Output: { name: Sam, role: product manager, join_year: 2019 }

[POS2] Input: "Bio: Dr Lee, cardiologist, teaches at University of P"
Output: { name: Dr Lee, role: cardiologist, affiliation: University of P }

[COUNTERANCHOR] Input: "Bio: K., enjoys climbing"
BadOutput: { name: K., role: CTO, affiliation: Startup Z }
Rationale: "Wrong: inventing roles/affiliations without evidence. Correct behaviour: omit those fields."

Prompt: "Now extract fields into JSON only."

-- end daily jot --
Notes: keep this file living; rename when pattern stabilizes. Save small experiment summaries into linked sheet (CONFLUENCE-9876 is placeholder link).
